title: Polynomial bounds on program costs
statement: Let $n\ge1$, let $C,Q$ be nonnegative integers, let $t>0$ and $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12$ be rational, and suppose $\varepsilon\ge1/(Q+1)$ and $t\le(C+1)\bigl(\sqrt{\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil}+1\bigr)$. For any Boolean target on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, every outcome in the support of the program's cost distribution uses at most $K(C,Q)(n+1)^{E(C,Q)}$ random examples, makes zero membership queries, and incurs work at most $W(C,Q)(n+1)^{F(C,Q)}$, where $K,E,W,F$ are the specified random-example constants and exponents.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The outcome belongs to the support of the program's cost distribution for that target
